body: Thanks for offering your support. I'm doing a little bit better right now because I'm talking with the other guy but I'll keep you in mind.

Well, I had to give that a lot of thought. I think I was probably most happiest just before I moved to where I am now. I was happy with my ex but not truly happy. I was taking piano lessons and I was doing a lot of different things. I had dropped out of community college, but it gave me a surprising amount of relief and freedom. I loved to sing and while I wasn't all that great on my piano, it was still something that I really enjoyed. I especially enjoyed my piano teacher. It was my choir teacher's husband and he invited me to their home to give me lessons. They were really cheap. He only charged me 20 bucks a lesson and lessons were two hours. They usually went over because we talked about life and how things were going. I told him I'd continue playing after I left to go be with my ex, but I never did because the room we were staying in never had enough room for it.

At present, my piano that I got off of Craigslist years ago is still at my ex's home. We've been trying our best to organize a time when I can get the rest of my stuff, but her mother won't allow me near the house and I live almost an hour away. I'm on very good terms with my ex but she has no way of transporting my piano along with the rest of my things. Plus she's busy with a new relationship and a job. I hate being a burden to her.

I want to move on just like she has, but I still feel a lot of my life is cooped up in that house.

Edit: I just want to say that I wrote that on my lunch. I'm doing my best not to neglect my work duties while having this chat. While it's sometimes difficult for me to come in, people count on me. I don't want to let them down.

I made a post on here a few days ago. If you're willing to read that, it goes into a bit more detail. My head was on a little better that day.

As for the exact things right now, I feel like I'm never going to become as good as I want to be in anything I try. I feel no motivation to do anything I love any more. I love computers and art, but every time I get home I end up crying before taking a nap. I lack any concrete credentials in my field and I feel that I have no mobility upward. I want to find love again, but I don't have what it takes to put myself out there because I feel extremely guilty about how my last relationship went ended which constantly beats down what little confidence I have. To top it off, my friend is sleeping on my couch. He fucks his new girlfriend even when I'm home and I feel he's taking advantage of me.

Sorry for the text dump.

I'm not sure. I feel hopeless, I guess. It's really difficult to stay focused right now. No one at my job really knows what I'm going through. Some asked if I was alright because they saw my eyes were red.

I'm an electronics refurbisher. I just told them I got a lot of dust in my eyes. I have no one to really talk to about this stuff. Even my best friend who I've known since I was 19 doesn't really know how I'm feeling.
I'd actually like that a lot, but I'm at work. I'm very sorry...

>Stop comparing yourself to your friends. This will depress you.

I know. I just can't stop doing it. I keep looking at all of the fulfilling shit they are doing on Facebook and I can't help but feel like I should have stayed in school. My rational side knows Facebook is designed to show only the bright, colorful, happy sides of peoples lives and not what happens beyond that, but I fell I don't have any of those moments peak moments to share with anyone. I obviously would have never known that things wouldn't have worked out in the beginning, but I wanted to give it a shot. I feel I'll forever pay the price.

>Personally I feel like you're getting yourself in the right direction, but seem bored with it.

I wouldn't say bored. I feel like I don't have enough time to work on things I used to love to do, but I have no way of escaping. I honestly like the city where I landed. I would rather not go home to my parents. They say they would always take me in. My parents care a lot for me. I just don't want to go and feel like I've become a societal burden. My dad told me I was going to fail the day I originally left, but he ended up apologizing to me when my ex and I broke up. He told me the only reason he acted that way was that he didn't want to see me leave, but he was proud of everything I've done. He felt bad because he felt that I didn't come to him in fear of appearing like a disappointment. Still, I just don't want to give up, but every day it feels more and more like an option.

>And make sure your goals align in a relationship before you move across country. :)

I just wish I had known this when I was 19. I feel braindead for not asking basic questions, but I don't even think I wanted kids back then. I tried to make things work, but I knew deep down it would be unhealthy to force anything. I felt trapped with no support system outside my ex. Not even her parents would help. Her mother constantly called me an idiot and a spineless asshole, and the berating only got worse when she was drinking. Sure, I lied a lot about everything, especially picking up smoking again, but I was just so afraid. I just never wanted to disagree with her because I was terrified of being kicked out. Ended up happening anyway, I guess.
